slides.title: Internal Relationships Deserve the Same Strategy
bullets: Internal stakeholders shape how much impact your work has, even excellent work
Commercial, market access, regulatory, clinical research, other MSLs and Medical Affairs leadership all matter
Treat internal relationships with the same intention as KOL and DOL engagement

slides.title: Understand Each Function's Priorities
bullets: Commercial is measured on short and medium term business results
Market access needs economic and clinical value evidence for reimbursement
Clinical research prioritizes methodological rigor and study timelines
Understand these priorities without adopting them as your own

slides.title: Build Regular, Not Just Reactive, Channels
bullets: Hold periodic alignment meetings with teams you collaborate with most often
Don't wait until a specific need arises to reach out
This builds the trust that makes collaboration easier under pressure

slides.title: Collaborate Without Losing Independence
bullets: Share insights and scientific context without compromising the role's non-promotional nature
Be clear internally about what can be shared, for what purpose, and through which channels
This stays consistent with the ethical principles covered earlier in the course

slides.title: Handle Disagreement With Evidence, Not Avoidance
bullets: Medical and commercial or market access perspectives will not always align
Address disagreement with evidence and the long-term interest of the product and patients
Seek constructive resolution instead of avoiding the conversation or imposing a position

slides.title: The Difference Between Influence and an Archive
bullets: Managing internal relationships well is not politics separate from medical work
It determines whether scientific knowledge translates into real organizational decisions
Done poorly, that knowledge stays archived without real influence

takeaway.title: Internal stakeholder management determines whether good science actually shapes decisions
bullets: Understanding each function's pressures makes your communication land better
Regular, proactive contact builds the trust that reactive contact never can
Handle disagreement with evidence while protecting Medical Affairs' independence
